question: A can do a work in 11 days and B can do the same work in 19 days. If they work on it together for 6 days, then what fraction of the work is left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = 11 × 19 = 209 units.

Combined efficiency = 19 + 11 = 30 units/day.

Work done in 6 days = 30 × 6 = 180 units.

Work left = 209 − 180 = 29 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 29/209.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 11 days

Time taken by B to complete the work = 19 days

They work together for 6 days.

 **Days**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 19 + 11 = 30 units/day

⇒ Work completed by A and B in 6 days = 30 × 6 = 180 units

⇒ Remaining work = 209 − 180 = 29 units

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining Work ÷ Total Work

⇒ Fraction of work left = 29 / 209

**∴ The correct answer is 29/209.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the work done by individuals. If they work for the same number of days, wages are shared in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and multiply by the maximum possible cycles to reach near the total work.

Pipes and Cisterns

It is similar to Time and Work. Inflow pipes have positive efficiency, and outflow (leakage) pipes have negative efficiency. Net efficiency is their algebraic sum.
